key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN surrogate model can accurately predict friction stir welding quality of HDPE and identify process windows that avoid defects.
engineering_relevance: The study gives practical welding guidelines by linking rotational speed, travel speed, and bottom preheating to thermal stability, axial force, and void formation in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE friction stir welding
Experimental validation across varying rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained to predict temperature and axial force responses
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values of 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental thermal, mechanical, and defect trends.
watch_item: The process maps are based on the tested HDPE parameter space, so broader use on other tool geometries, thicknesses, or polymers may require retraining and revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
